Trucker who crashed off Pascagoula River Bridge identified, cause still unknown
item.description: A tractor-trailer driver, identified as 64-year-old Norberto Barahona-Mejia of Conroe, Texas, died after his truck left the Pascagoula River Bridge on I-10 in Jackson County, Mississippi, on November 17. According to a report citing WKRG, the crash happened around 12:15 a.m., after the truck collided with a Honda Accord that was also eastbound, and the trailer went over the side of the bridge into the water below. The 27-year-old driver of the Honda Accord and a 28-year-old passenger were injured and are expected to make full recoveries. Officials are still investigating, and the cause has not been released.

Bot Auto launches ‘Capacity Grid’ with agreements for 200 million miles of driverless trucking
item.description:
Bot Auto has launched Capacity Grid, a network intended to match shipper and broker demand with driverless trucking capacity, and has signed agreements covering 200 million miles of driverless freight operations. Customers can reserve capacity for set routes and time windows at agreed prices, buying transportation by the mile without owning trucks. FreightVana, a logistics company specializing in power-only freight transportation, has a commitment covering 50 million miles.
The company said a driverless load ran from northeast Houston to Hutchins, near Dallas, on April 29, covering 231 miles for Ryan Transportation. Figures reported by the company put the driverless trip at $1.89 per mile, against $3.78 for a comparable human-driven operation within its business. Bot Auto has not specified when the full 200 million miles will be completed.

13 suspects charged in $22M freight train cargo theft scheme in US
item.description: Thirteen men were charged Thursday over an alleged freight train theft operation that prosecutors say took more than $22 million in cargo bound for major retailers. A federal indictment unsealed the same day says the suspects targeted more than 36 trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear and power tools that came through the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. Prosecutors allege the group disabled trains by damaging their braking systems at set locations, then moved the goods onto trucks. The merchandise was sold to an unidentified company that allegedly resold it. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli called the alleged thefts "staggering" and promised further prosecutions in similar cases. All 13 defendants face conspiracy and theft of interstate railroad cargo charges, and two of them also face a count involving violence against railroad carriers. If convicted, they could face federal prison terms of five to 20 years.

At least 36 Southern California trains burglarised in $22.5 million cargo theft racket; 14 accused allege
item.description:
The US Department of Justice said 14 people have been indicted over alleged thefts of more than $22.5 million in cargo from freight trains in Southern California. According to the DOJ, the group burglarised at least three dozen trains between February 2024 and August 2026, taking goods that included Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools. Investigators allege members cut air hoses to force emergency stops, then boarded the trains and removed valuable cargo.
Thirteen of the 14 defendants were arrested on Thursday, and the case is a 17-count federal indictment. Investigators allege two defendants sold thousands of pairs of stolen Nike sneakers to a Los Angeles resale business, receiving approximately $1,081,493 between May and October 2025. The alleged leader is identified as Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles. All defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

Truck driver arrested after he was caught hauling oversized load at night with no permit and suspended CDL, Missouri sheriff says
item.description: A Platte County Sheriff's Office deputy in Missouri arrested a truck driver after stopping an oversized load on I-29 at night without warning devices or banners. The deputy found the driver's commercial driver license suspended and no oversized load permit from the Missouri Department of Transportation, and the load was reported to be over 13 feet wide. The inspection also recorded eight Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulation violations, and the Louisiana for-hire motor carrier and driver were placed out of service. Two days after the driver posted bond, the same deputy stopped the same load on Route 92. This time it had warning devices and banners, but still no MoDOT permit, and 15 violations were recorded. A court summons was issued, and the driver was helped to obtain a permit.

Dallas College, Goodwill Expand CDL Training Program
item.description: Dallas College and Goodwill Dallas have teamed up with FleetForce Truck Driver Training to widen CDL instruction across Dallas-Fort Worth. The program covers Class A, B and C licenses and combines classroom work with hands-on training, with FleetForce instructors teaching at Goodwill facilities. The Dallas location is FleetForce's 17th in the U.S. The company's Next10,000 campaign aims to train 10,000 students through 2026 and cites about 6,100 local CDL openings in the region. Qualified graduates are guaranteed an interview with a large full-truckload carrier through FleetForce's Pre-Hire network. The article does not yet give enrollment figures or completion and placement rates for Dallas students.

Unsafe truck drivers could be publicly outed under new Alberta law
item.description: Alberta's government is proposing Bill 43, the Safe and Sensible Roads Act, which would amend the province's Traffic Safety Act to toughen penalties for unsafe trucking. Under the bill, fines for unsafe commercial truck operators would rise from $10,000 to $50,000 for violations including repeated safety breaches and bridge strikes. Driver licences could also be cut to a basic Class 5 licence or made subject to conditions after serious incidents such as a bridge strike. Transportation Minister Devin Dreeshen said retraining would be required before a driver returns to regular duties. If the bill passes, the government would publish information on non-compliant carriers, drivers, driving schools, inspection facilities and company owners and directors. Separately, a Calgary Police Service blitz in September pulled 100 of 197 stopped commercial vehicles off the road for critical defects. In March, a truck hauling equipment struck a rail bridge in Lethbridge, knocking concrete loose and leading to costly repairs for the municipality.
